subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Perhaps the Minister of
National Defence for Naval Affairs could answer my question with regard to the training of men for merchant ships?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: This matter really does not come under the Department of National Defence for Naval Services; it belongs rather to the Department of Transport. I do not know of any plans having been made by the government for the training of men for merchant ships. The suggestion has been made that some attention should be given to the formation of manning pools in various parts of the country, so that merchant seamen may be allotted to those ships which may be short of crews.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Is there any restriction on the use of wooden ships with diesel engines? This is a matter of great concern to Nova Scotia. Many of these
ships can travel just as fast as steam transports.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I do not know that there is any restriction in the formal sense, but as far as convoy work is concerned I do not think anyone would think of using ships of wooden ship size. I doubt if anyone would think of a ship of less than 6,000, 7,000 or 10,000 tons, and with those sizes you are out of the wooden ship class. The opinion of naval men and of those engaged in merchant shipping is that for convoy work you cannot have a great number of small ships because they are as much trouble as a large ship.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: The controlling factor would be speed rather than size, would it not?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: They are slow ships, generally speaking.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I should like to direct a question to the Minister of Mines and Resources (Mr. Crerar). I notice that there is an item of $147,000 under this department to provide for the detention of alien seamen who refuse to perform their regular duties in Canada. There are rumours to the effect that in some parts of Canada the reason for this refusal is the fact that the government has offered them lower rates of wages than are paid to Canadian seamen. Last summer there were some 200 French seamen off four or five French boats which had been brought into Sydney from the banks and tied up in the harbour. These men were roaming around apparently without any supervision or means of livelihood, and most of them could not speak the language of the country. Was anything done for this particular group of men? In just what way .is this $147,000 to be spent?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: When my hon. friend says that the government offered them a lower wage than they have been receiving, that must be incorrect because the government does not operate any transatlantic steamship service, and the pay of merchant seamen is entirely a matter between the seamen and the shipping company which employs them.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: These men being detained by the government, the government would have something to say with respect to their employment.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
The government would have nothing to say with respect to their employment. They were detained, I presume, for some offence under the Canada Shipping Act. The government would have nothing to say as to the rate of wages because they are not government
War Appropriation Bill

employees in the same sense that men in the navy are. The government does not operate a merchant marine service across the Atlantic.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: If I might add a word to what my colleague has said, sometimes we find sailors deserting their ship when it reaches Canadian shores, and then they come under our immigration laws. We insist that they shall return to their ship, and if they do not they are taken into custody. These sailors are of many nationalities, and a great majority of them cannot be deported to their own country. Consequently they are detained in custody in Canada until they express a willingness to return to their vocation as sailors. This sum of money is to cover the necessary expenses incidental thereto.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Can the minister give us the number of these men, their nationality and the names of the ships they deserted?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I cannot give that information now, but I could probably get a fairly accurate summary prepared.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: The sailors I spoke of did not desert their ships, but the ships were detained in Sydney harbour for some months. Perhaps they are still there. The 200 sailors were not detained but were moving about from place to place, living pretty much on the charity of anyone who would take them in.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Didn't they sell their fish in Sydney?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I do not know. My connection with them was to try to secure relief for them, and I was wondering how that group of men was taken care of. Their ships were detained and they were prohibited from taking employment anywhere.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
I should like to ask a question of the Minister of Trade and Commerce. The Ottawa Journal of March 17 last has an article headed "Teachers Offer to Take Census Free of Cost". It goes on to say:
The Canadian Federation of Teachers volunteered to take the census free of cost to the government, it was announced on Saturday by Miss Eleanor Anderson, president.
Miss Anderson was speaking at the annual meeting of the federation of women teachers for districts 12 and 13, in the Chateau Laurier. She said no reply to the offer of voluntary help had been received.
She thought most of the appointments had already been made and were likely to be political. Miss Anderson told the Journal that
25,000	teachers in Ontario alone were available for census work and would like to undertake it in June.
My question is, does the government consider it an essential part of the war effort to take the census at this time? And has the government refused the offer of the Canadian

Federation of Teachers, which would save the country approximately 83,000,000 at this time? We know that census commissioners have already been appointed on a patronage basis. Will the minister say on what basis the enumerators will be selected?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Just before my colleague answers, I want to enter a protest, Mr. Chairman, against this discussion going any further than is necessary at this time. There is an item in the main estimates covering the census and the discussion on the census should take place on that item, not on this clause. If we get into a discussion on that subject now, there is nothing to prevent us from giving the rest of the week to it if some of the members continue the practice of the last few weeks. If my colleague desires to answer to oblige the hon. member, and then the matter is let go at that, I have no objection, but I certainly would object to the committee entering upon a discussion of the census under this clause.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: That will be quite satisfactory to me. To take the census would cost a lot of money, and I thought, therefore, my question had a bearing when we are now voting this large sum for the war.

Section agreed to.
Section 3 agreed to.
On section 4-Loans authorized.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: The minister has not in any way divided the amounts which may be raised by loan and by taxation. I know this is the exact wording that was used in last year's bill, but I think some restriction should be placed on the total amount that can be borrowed and on the amount to be raised by taxation. The whole $1,300,000,000 could be borrowed under this clause. It is too wide, and I want to enter a formal protest against that kind of procedure.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Before the clause
carries, I want to take this opportunity of doing something which was declared out of order when the resolution was before the house. ,

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Will the hon. gentleman do me the favour of giving me a few minutes before eleven o'clock to present supplementary estimates to the house?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I shall be very glad to give way to the minister now because what I have to say would take until eleven o'clock.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
